heading: 4.1a.1 What a perfusion measurement is

sentence: DOI `10.1093/bja/aei095`. — **`FULL TEXT HELD`****.** Contributes: eight concentrations from 0.008% to 0.75%; **net vasoconstriction only at 0.008–0.031%, with 0.0625% ≈ saline**; every epinephrine-containing response below saline; the Åberg calcium-mobilisation/membrane-stabilisation mechanism; the iontophoresis finding that 0.5% sodium chloride has no vasodilatory effect in human skin; and the reason pinprick was not attempted.

heading: 15.1 Vessels in skin — the core
sentence: Epub 20 Aug 2007. — **`FULL TEXT HELD`****.** Contributes: the biphasic window 3 × 10⁻⁵ to 3 × 10⁻⁴ M with relaxation from 10⁻³; the nicardipine/2-APB dissection and its additivity; **the tension/calcium dissociation implying a calcium-independent arm**; the explicit conversion of the clinical range to (0.6–2.4) × 10⁻² M; **the statement that clinical concentrations appear too high to contract vascular smooth muscle**; the interstitial-dilution reconciliation; and the statement that **local injected concentration has never been measured** — **a statement that was true of the vascular literature but is false in general; see Kimi 2012 and Yamashiro 2016 in 4.5, which this page previously missed.** Limits: rat aorta, a conductance vessel; endothelium-denuded; in vitro; relaxation at high concentration acknowledged as unexplained.

heading: 15.2 Duration
sentence: Limits: 18 volunteers; five times a wheal’s volume; vasoconstriction observed, not measured.

heading: 15.2 Duration
sentence: Standing: 48 citing publications, 36 classified statements — 1 supporting, 1 contrasting, no editorial notices; the contrasting statement concerns onset time in a dental study, and **no paper has contradicted the 21.5-hour duration.**

heading: 15.4 Neurotoxicity
sentence: All four produced a **concentration-dependent increase in every measure of injury.** Injury predominantly subperineurial. **The Schwann cells of unmyelinated fibres were more likely to undergo lysis; those of myelinated fibres to accumulate cytoplasmic lipid droplets.** The finding most specific to small fibre neuropathy in the whole collection — but **ropivacaine was not tested.**

heading: 15.4 Neurotoxicity
sentence: DOI `10.17245/jdapm.2020.20.2.63`. — **`ABSTRACT`****.** 2,802 hits screened, 23 eligible: 17 in vitro studies, 3 reviews, 3 national-inquiry audits. **“All dental local anesthetics are potentially neurotoxic in a concentration and/or exposure time fashion”** and **“there is no unanimity in the publications about which local anesthetic is the least or the most neurotoxic.”** Notes there is no consensus on which cell lines to use, which makes comparison between studies ambiguous. **This is the honest summary of section 6.1 and should be quoted to the human when the toxicity ranking comes up.**

heading: Ectopic firing — the concentration separation
sentence: The only paper in this collection giving the separation as a percentage.** In vivo rat, epidural application to the DRG surface: **0.02% or 0.2% lidocaine substantially suppressed DRG electrogenesis with only a modest effect on impulse propagation through the foramen.** Topical opiates and GABA blocked neither.

heading: Ectopic firing — the concentration separation
sentence: **Kankel J et al. 2012**, “Differential effects of low dose lidocaine on C-fiber classes in humans”; and **Miclescu A et al. 2015**, DOI `10.1016/j.sjpain.2015.04.026`. — **`CITATION ONLY`****, neither obtained.** Named by an independent audit as **the human microneurography entry points** and the closest available approach to the missing experiment: recording a cutaneous C-fibre during a local anaesthetic wheal in a person. **Worth obtaining if the endpoint argument in 5.6 ever needs to rest on human data.**
